Per-patient control spread across propensity models

Source: R/control_spread.R
control_spread.Rd

For each treated patient, collect the distinct untreated partners matched to it by the models in use and compute s, the mean pairwise Mahalanobis distance between their covariate vectors, with the covariance matrix of all n patients. s = 0 when every model picks the same untreated partner, and NA when the patient is unmatched in every model. s_scaled = s / D, where D is the mean over matched treated patients of the Mahalanobis distance between a treated patient and its logistic-regression match (the first model in use when the match set has no logistic regression model): 1 means the candidate partners differ from each other as much as a typical match differs from its treated patient. The oracle entry and the bootstrap block are never used.

Usage

control_spread(match_set, covariates, use_gate = TRUE, models = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'control_spread'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

match_set

A match_set from match_each_model().

covariates

A data frame with one row per patient, in the data's row order, holding the covariates that define the distance (usually those of the propensity formula).

use_gate

TRUE (default) to use the models that passed the log-loss gate; FALSE to use every model.

models

Optional character vector of model ids to use instead of a gate; it overrides use_gate. The wrapper propensity_sensitivity() passes the final quality-gate set (log-loss and balance) this way.

x

A control_spread object.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "control_spread": a list with patients (one row per patient: row, id, treated, distinct_controls, control_spread, control_spread_scaled; NA for untreated patients), summary (mean_scaled_treated, p90_scaled_treated, scale_distance, scale_model), models_used, quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models and settings (with the dropped columns).

Covariates

Factors and logical columns are expanded to dummies (treatment contrasts). Character columns are an error: convert them to factors. Constant columns and linearly dependent columns (found with a pivoted QR decomposition of the standardized design) are dropped with a message. The Mahalanobis distance is sqrt((a - b)' S^-1 (a - b)), the square root of what stats::mahalanobis() returns.

Quality gate

With use_gate = TRUE only the models that passed the log-loss gate are used. If fewer than two passed, all models are used and quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models is TRUE . The flag reports the gate's outcome whatever use_gate is.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
model_set <- fit_propensity_models(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, seeds = 1, n_trees = 100,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting")
)
match_set <- match_each_model(model_set, lalonde, replace = TRUE)
covariates <- lalonde[, c("age", "educ", "race", "married", "nodegree", "re74", "re75")]
spread <- control_spread(match_set, covariates)
spread
#> Control spread: 2 model(s) in use (after the log-loss gate)
#> Scaled control spread over treated: mean 1.035, 90th percentile 1.927
#> Scale: mean Mahalanobis distance treated to match under logistic_regression_1 = 2.584
head(spread$patients[spread$patients$treated == 1, ])
#>   row   id treated distinct_controls control_spread control_spread_scaled
#> 1   1 NSW1       1                 2      4.3937831             1.7004394
#> 2   2 NSW2       1                 2      5.8022919             2.2455468
#> 3   3 NSW3       1                 1      0.0000000             0.0000000
#> 4   4 NSW4       1                 2      2.4397568             0.9442110
#> 5   5 NSW5       1                 2      0.9652184             0.3735495
#> 6   6 NSW6       1                 2      2.1516074             0.8326943
